newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila launches $12.75 bln plan for armed forces.
newsitem.headline: Manila launches $12.75 bln plan for armed forces.

text.p: The Philippines on Thursday launched a 15-year plan to modernise its armed forces, with President Fidel Ramos signing a congressional resolution appropriating $12.75 billion for the programme.

The modernisation programme, partly dictated by concerns about possible conflicts over disputed South China Sea islands, calls for purchases of frigates, jet fighters, armoured vehicles and weaponry to boost the country's defence requirements.
No contracts for military hardware have yet been signed but officials say several defence delegations have visited Western nations with lists of requirements.
The resolution, approved by the Senate and the House of Representatives, sets aside 50 billion pesos ($1.9 billion) to finance the first five years of the programme.

"This is not only a timely but a very appropriate Christmas gift to the nation," Ramos said while signing the resolution. "In due time, we shall have a modern armed force -- one that deserves our people's respect, our neighbours' high regard...."

Part of the funds will be used to set up new military bases and upgrade existing facilities in the western region of the country, "the area where the most probable threat is to come from," a military statement on the programme said.

It did not say what the threat might be but a "primer on modernisation" released by the defence department specified the Spratly Islands in the South China Sea as a potential source of conflict in case oil was discovered in the area.

The Spratlys are a cluster of isles, reefs and shoals believed to be sitting atop rich oil and gas deposits and are claimed wholly or in part by China, Taiwan, Vietnam, the Philippines, Malaysia and Brunei.
The navy and air force, considered the most vulnerable areas in the country's defence system, are to receive the biggest share of the 331.62-billion-peso ($12.75-billion) modernisation budget.

To upgrade the navy, the Philippines plans to buy more patrol boats, frigates, corvettes and missile boats while getting attack aircraft, jet fighters, helicopters and surface-to-air missile systems for the air force, the military document said.
The programme also calls for purchases of artillery systems and armoured vehicles for the army and training of military personnel.
